topics.topic: How instance-selection/address runtime subcases map to `instance_not_selected` vs `instance_address_missing` and what input `prepare_request` needs to decide
questions: How does `prepare_request` receive the selected instance *name* (needed to distinguish `instance_not_selected` from `instance_address_missing`) if its declared inputs include only ManifestOperation-with-facts?
Exactly which runtime subcases map to `instance_not_selected` vs `instance_address_missing` (including selected instance name missing from manifest, missing instance entry fields, or invalid URL)?

quotes:
A ManifestOperation M10 with instance facts — its `service_id` names the
service — the binding's input and output Ports, and the element's input values
and file bytes by port.

State 3 order after the binding: no selected instance (no name), no
`api_base_url` (a name without one), a repeated required header, a plain `http`
target not allowed, then the credential, then input placement, input ports in
name order and a list's elements in list order, the first that cannot be placed
named (A09 rules 1, 2, 4, 6); credential by name only in the description (A10
rule 7); the description covers every header sent on the wire, and no header is
sent that it does not describe; one `host` header, the instance's required
`host` when it names one, else the authority of `api_base_url` (A10 rule 7); a `GET` or `DELETE` list input that is empty
adds no query parameter (A09 rule 2).

The current ManifestOperation M10 — and beside it, not in it, the selected
instance's name — with that instance's `base_url`, `required_headers` and
`instance_class` as read — the name absent when none is selected, the others
absent when missing — or `binding_stale` for any failure of the record itself
(A08 rule 6).
judgement.divergence: Behavior A: `effects` passes only ManifestOperation data into `prepare_request`, so absent/invalid address subcases collapse and implementation may always emit `instance_address_missing` when instance facts are absent; Behavior B: `effects` also passes the selected instance name returned by `check_binding_current`, so `prepare_request` emits `instance_not_selected` when no name is selected and `instance_address_missing` only when a selected instance lacks/has invalid address facts; the owner/agent notices via different `operation_failed` detail codes.
judgement.why: The texts require distinct runtime details but do not close exactly what input `prepare_request` receives and the exact mapping of all missing/invalid instance-address subcases to those details.

topics.topic: Which services `bindings.check_installed_instances` must iterate at startup (including services without a selected instance) and failure behavior for unreadable manifest records
questions: At start, does `check_installed_instances` validate services with no selected instance, and should an unreadable manifest record for such a service stop startup?
Which services are included in this ordered check set at startup?

quotes:
`service_instances`: at most one selected instance per service, by its
  manifest instance name; a service with none selected is not invocable, and
  a binding for it is refused when proposed or accepted, its ManifestOperation
  then read without instance facts (A17 rule 4, A08 rules 5 and 7);

`refused` naming the first failing service, services taken in `service_id`
code-point order and each one's manifest record read in its turn — an
unreadable record fails at its service; the start stops.
judgement.divergence: Behavior A: `bindings.check_installed_instances` iterates all services known in installation configuration (including services with no selected instance), so an unreadable manifest for such a service stops startup; Behavior B: it iterates only services with a selected instance, so unreadable manifests for unselected services are ignored and startup can proceed; the owner/operator notices whether the kernel starts and which service is named as first failure.
judgement.why: The check order is specified, but the service set to iterate at startup is left open while startup success/failure depends on that choice.

topics.topic: Canonical identity model for `SpooledFile` records (full-value identity vs positional lookup tuple)
questions: Is the canonical identity of a SpooledFile the full fact set (value identity) or the positional tuple used by `read_spooled_file` and store lookups?

topics.topic: Exact addressing schema for operation elements in effects APIs (`reach_operation_element` / `operation_element_conclusion`)
questions: What exact fields identify "node and element" for `effects.reach_operation_element` and `effects.operation_element_conclusion` (node_id only, node_id+map_index, plus binding_id/effect_class, etc.)?

topics.topic: How `store.record_change` must handle acting Actor data when target record types have no actor fields
questions: What is the required behavior for the acting Actor when the target records do not have actor fields: persist it somewhere, or drop it?

topics.topic: How per-attempt spool rollback is guaranteed across multiple `spool_file` calls when a later file exceeds a ceiling
questions: Given `spool_file` takes one file per call, how is "any file that attempt spooled before" guaranteed to be removed when a later file in the same attempt crosses a ceiling?

topics.topic: Required JSON parsing/canonicalization strategy to detect and reject duplicate object keys in surface requests
questions: How must surface parse incoming JSON so duplicate object keys are detectable and refused, rather than silently collapsed by a normal JSON parser?

topics.topic: What `attempt_number` callers must supply to `store.spool_file` before run-progress/read-outcome persistence assigns the attempt
questions: Before `record_run_progress` / `record_read_outcome` writes the NodeExecution (where `store` assigns the next attempt number), what exact attempt_number must callers pass to `store.spool_file` for files produced by function nodes and `read` operation nodes?

topics.topic: Whether `internal_error` is a refusal result or a separate non-refusal error class in module API contracts
questions: Is `internal_error` part of the refusal channel or a separate non-refusal result class for module APIs?
